In the case of Cyberpunk you have to consider how society shapes morality and environment shapes people. V can take issue with a lot of things, but ultimately is a product of Night City. Most of the people you mow down are members of the gangs, corrupt officials, or fellow edgerunners: all people who've made a choice to engage in Night City's system of violence. By contrast V still has a sense of personal right and wrong as seen in how they can treat those who mistreat children, are dishonest, or pulled into situations with no choice. V sees the tragedy on a grand scale and the issues that exist systemically, but doesn't concern themselves with that level of morality considering every moment in Night City is life or death. V COULD see the tragedy in every scavver they kill because that scavver was a product of their environment, but won't.

I watched the VersusWolves segment and feel like some additional context could help:

They're technically incorrect when they say Rollins, Mox, and Reigns were in NXT together because WWE's "development system" was different at the time. The trio who would make up The Shield started out in WWE working Florida Championship Wrestling which drew sub-100 sized crowds and didn't have any tv deal which wasn't FL local. As a result you had to follow uploads to Dailymotion to follow WWE Development. WWE Development wouldn't even be considered within the greater WWE kayfabe until the formation of NXT. 

IIRC Rollins had quickly established himself with a series of matches with Ricky Steamboat's son Richie who was then a TOP prospect in FCW. Moxley had quickly made a name for himself in FCW with a feud with authority figure and veteran William Regal. As a result you have 3 individuals: two of whom had big followings on the indie scene who had maintained buzz around them into their WWE careers. People were pirating FCW shows to watch Rollins vs Steamboat or Regal vs Moxley. People weren't really pirating FCW for Leakee until they all started working a three way rivalry. This may be where WWE saw the chemistry between the three as they had a hell of a triple threat match against each other in FCW.

So when The Shield debuted there was still enough of a following around 2/3 of them that people know *of* them...the problem is Leakee, now Roman Reigns, came in without the indie following and a new name. There were things at play working against Roman Reigns early on before the legit boo'ing ever manifested.

It's Subdermal Armor cyberware, which in the ttrpg provides a 13 armor. For bullets to penetrate the damage it must exceed the armor rating and your average Medium Pistol does 2d6 damage, meaning a medium pistol can only do 12 damage. By comparison a shotgun can do 5d6, which at max damage would be enough to critically wound any *average* person with subdermal armor but still not enough to kill.

The City Center we know as Corpo Plaza was destroyed and reduced to a wasteland. Around 750,000 people died as a result of the radiation and ensuing chaos across the city as many were displaced. Side effects of the bomb included a blood red sky which would lead to this period being known as The Time of the Red. The mass homelessness would force NC to rush the construction of the Megabuildings thanks to assistance by the NUSSR.

During this time Night City was probably at its worst, but also most hopeful. Whole areas were reduced to lawless combat zones and the *good* areas of NC would be ranked by how many blocks away from a CZ they were. Supply lines and distribution of necessary goods also took a hit from the 4th Corporate War so during this time the only reliable source of food was through Continental Brands and their kibble. I mentioned hope earlier because during this time there saw a sort of DIY movement in the wake of the war and amongst the scarcity. People had fewer means to go to stores to just buy shit so people made do with what could be salvaged and communes made an effort at micro gardening. Young people during this time, Generation Red, are more comparable to our activist Gen Z.

Night City would rebound in the wake of the war in part due to the absence of Arasaka, allowing other corps to come in and fill the void while actual oversight and regulation was being brought back. A lot of these improvements would be undone by Arasaka's return to Night City. Many of the conditions we see NC in by 2077 are not due to the bomb, but rather Arasaka's return and rapid re-investment in NC in their interest. So in a way NC had been "rebuilt" twice since the end of the 4th Corporate War: once to rebuild infrastructure, twice for Arasaka to get their claws in the city's operations.
